restrictions: Classical probabilistic 256-bit word RAM under collision-frontier-v5 (C = 2224); total work over all processors, including the characteristic search (charged as an itemised allowance of 2^25.02 solver thread CPU-seconds at 2^23 units per CPU-second = 2^48.02 units, anchored to 247,285 measured thread CPU-seconds), the starting-solution search (2^37.83 units) and the statically audited table build (charged as 2^39.5 units), all in preprocessing.

Two-block messages M0||M1 and M0||M1' of 128 bytes; complete SHA-256 with standard IV, steps 0..31 on all three padded blocks, feed-forward and all 256 digest bits; outputs verified by full recomputation and accompanied by a verified 128-byte 32-step collision certificate.

32-step truncation of the 35-step attack of Li, Liu, Wang, Shi (CRYPTO 2026, ePrint 2026/1080), using its Fig. 6 characteristic and starting solution as advice; truncation, table and Step-2/3 tests follow hash-smash #26/#33 (winglock), re-implemented and re-measured in #296 (mitchuski), with the certified 32-step witness and deterministic compact-table slice replay from #227 (yudduy). The replay proves one witness lineage and does not validate the current 27-bit table cardinalities, completeness or build cost.

One run of T = ceil(2^44.83) = 31,273,371,622,600 independent first-block trials with a counted Step-2/3 work cap of 300 T word operations; the bucket scan is reserved once and every later charged tranche is checked against the remaining cap before execution, with one rejected check charged separately and no restarts. Under the declared per-trial success and work-moment premises, success exceeds 0.3955. Using the rounded online bound, total work A + B + C + D + E < 2^45.05 + 2^39.5 + 2^37.83 + 2^48.020 < 2^48.1979 < 2^48.20 units; preprocessing is below 2^48.0252 < 2^48.05. This early-abort accounting refinement adapts public Yukon submission f15d0743-ef0b-4b1e-83ba-6beae0fb9d9a (PR #395, score 48.21), which adapts a36add2f-5e05-4c9c-a727-eae03adc7be4 and 491c0048-2712-407c-beeb-207de0284c89; it keeps the same collision route, trial cap and probability premises while separating the measured stage-16 and stage-17 work.

Heuristic bound: relies on the declared heuristics q-32step-matching-rate, step3-46-conditions, attack-work-moments, precomputation-op-cap, route-search-allowance, cpu-second-pricing and valid-tuple-pairs (score-critical), plus starting-solution-measured and search-peak-memory (supporting).

heuristics.statement: A uniform first block M0 compressed with C_32 from the IV yields at least 2^-17.3584 expected valid tuples (Step 2) against TAB2 of 1,396,774,912 tuples.
heuristics.scope: The exact TAB2 and Step-2 tests of proof Section 4 with C_32 first blocks.
heuristics.extrapolation: Exact-enumeration prediction 2^-17.3254; four measured runs, 2^34 part-trials and 25,936 valid tuples give pooled q_hat = 25,936/2^32 = 2^-17.3373. A one-sided normal approximation to the summed rare-event counts gives the 99% lower bound (25,936 - 2.32635 sqrt(25,936))/2^32 = 2^-17.3583236, rounded downward here to 2^-17.3584. The retained tuple slice replay verifies one fixed derivation but does not estimate q.
heuristics.limitations: Large-scale rate runs are participant C executions; treats CV1 words as uniform for the Step-2 tests.

heuristics.statement: The declared heuristic premise is that, for a valid tuple, each of the 196,608 (W14,W15) candidates conforms through step 22 and W16..W31 with probability at least 2^-46, and Step 3 succeeds with r >= 3 * 2^-30 (1 - 2^-20).
heuristics.scope: Steps 16..22 and W16..W31 of the second block; candidates grouped by W14 (12 groups of 2^14), with that grouping used in the Bonferroni pair correction for r.
heuristics.extrapolation: Measured cumulative stage rates through step 21 over 2^32.25 candidates match the condition mapping. The 13 later conditions are extrapolated; the certified 128-byte witness and fixed replay demonstrate feasibility of one full conformance, not its rate.
heuristics.limitations: Independence beyond the W14 grouping is not proved; the 13 W20/W22 carry conditions after step 21 are extrapolated from the condition count. The single certified witness demonstrates feasibility only and supplies no rate evidence.

heuristics.statement: For scoring, the search that produced the published 35-step characteristic (S Sect. 3-4) is assigned a declared heuristic allowance of 2^25.02 solver thread CPU-seconds on the measurement machine (2^48.02 units at 2^23 units per CPU-second).
heuristics.scope: Characteristic search only; charged once as preprocessing; its memory is declared under search-peak-memory.
heuristics.extrapolation: Itemised from measured data: 247,285 thread CPU-s (48,912 wall-s) for Steps 1-4 as run under /usr/bin/time -v (which already sums user+sys CPU time across all solver threads); Step-4 completion estimated at 0.2M-4.0M thread CPU-s (subtotal 4.25M < 2^22.02 thread CPU-s); multiplied by x8 for S's selection loop (3.40e7 < 2^25.02 thread CPU-s, > 135x the entire 57-call run) without double-counting the thread factor. Declared plausible, not established.
heuristics.limitations: S's own search time is unpublished and no run here reproduced Fig. 6; the Step-4 completion estimate and selection-loop factor of 8 are argued envelopes, not direct measurements.

heuristics.statement: One solver CPU-second on the measurement machine costs at most 2^23 target-compression units (2^34.12 primitive 256-bit word-RAM operations, 17.0 operations per retired instruction).
heuristics.scope: The STP+CryptoMiniSat runs of the characteristic and starting-solution searches.
heuristics.extrapolation: Measured 2^30.03 instructions per CPU-second (callgrind count of a deterministic call against native CPU time) and opcode mix (multiply/divide/floating point 0.42%, unmapped 7.24%) leave 17.0 primitive 256-bit word-RAM operations per instruction at kappa = 2^23 (as in #134), with full sensitivity at 2^24 and 2^25 reported in Section 8.
heuristics.limitations: One single-thread calibration instance; instruction rate under the run's machine load.

heuristics.statement: E[C(V,2)] <= q * 2^-5 for the number V of valid tuples in one trial.
heuristics.scope: Valid tuples sharing one first block.
heuristics.extrapolation: 9 within-part pairs in 2^34 part-trials; cross-part term estimated from multiplicity sums with the observed correlation factor; charge exceeds the estimate by more than 20x.

heuristics.statement: For the counted Step-2/3 work X of one first-block trial under the stage-16/stage-17 early-abort schedule, E[X] <= 211.3 and E[X^2] <= 4.18e12; across independently sampled first blocks the work variables are independent enough that Var(sum X_i) <= T E[X^2].
heuristics.scope: The Step-2/3 work counter in proof Section 8 and its hard cap W_cap = 300 T for T independent first-block trials; candidates stop after a failed stage 16 or stage 17 before later work.
heuristics.extrapolation: The mean combines measured bucket occupancy, the exact table-cardinality rate N/2^32 < 0.32522, Step-2 pass fractions, the q upper confidence bound, f16 <= 0.126, and f17 <= 2^-14.9, conservatively above the measured 0.1250002 and cumulative stage-17 rate 155,619/(25,936*196,608) = 2^-14.999972. The charged candidate tranches are 48 operations at stage 16, 256 after stage 16 and 2,048 after stage 17; their worst-case sum is 2,352, with explicit slack above audited subtotals 32, 194 and 1,866. The second moment combines that padded maximum with the maximum bucket occupancy, tuple multiplicity sum, q upper bound and declared grouping; the displayed terms sum below 4.176e12 and are rounded upward to 4.18e12. Chebyshev bounds cap stop by 4.18e12 / ((300 - 211.3)^2 T) < 1.70e-5.
heuristics.limitations: The rate and moment inputs are participant measurements rather than organizer executions; the bound assumes the claimed random first-block trials transfer those distributions independently and inherits the unobserved cross-part tuple-pair premise.

heuristics.statement: The finite no-sort P1-P4 reference pseudocode requires at most 1,383,308,004,307,968 primitive word operations, equal to 621,991,009,131.2806 < 2^39.178103 target-compression units, and is charged at 2^39.5 units.
heuristics.scope: The one-time 27-bit-bucket TAB2 and P4 construction charged as term C in proof Section 8, including both W7 passes, record actions, fixed-array administration, bucket zeroing/prefix/cursor checks and auxiliary rows.
heuristics.extrapolation: Static worst-case source audit: 168,209,023,232 exact main iterations are each charged 8,192 operations after phase-by-phase helper expansion; every W7 candidate in one complete pass receives a separate 64-operation record-action charge; each of 2^27+1 bucket boundaries receives 1,024 operations covering both count/cursor and offset arrays; and every retained auxiliary row receives another 1,024 operations. The exact integer sum is divided by C=2224 and rounded up to 2^39.5.
heuristics.limitations: The exact table cardinalities are inherited participant enumerations from #26/#296. The audit is for the displayed prospective fixed-capacity, no-sort word-RAM pseudocode; it is not a compilable historical source file, native instruction trace, wall-time measurement or organizer full build. Different predicates, capacities, dynamic growth or sorting invalidate the bound.

heuristics.statement: Producing the starting solution costs at most 32 x 908.8 CPU-seconds (two measured SAT runs) at 2^23 units per CPU-second (2^37.83 units), above S's reported 2^34.3 in any unit up to one compression.
heuristics.scope: The advice values A4..A13, E8..E13, W12, W13.
heuristics.extrapolation: Two SAT runs of S's attack Step 1 task (solution through step 13, checked exactly), the second with S's printed single-bit conditions asserted; S's own solution is the advice.
heuristics.limitations: Comparability of our solution to S's is neither claimed nor needed; the anchor is the cost of the same task.

heuristics.statement: The route search (S's and ours) needs at most 2^33 bytes at its peak.
heuristics.scope: Memory of the characteristic and starting-solution searches, which run before the attack phase.
heuristics.extrapolation: Measured peak resident set 5.25 GiB over all 57 search calls and both start runs; S's own search is assumed of the same model size.
heuristics.limitations: S's historical peak is not reported; the measured peaks are added to the memory bound anyway.
